ruling.recommended_action: Refund $7.47 (RydeTAXI excess-distance component of the unexempt detour) to the rider as a voucher; issue no account flag (driver's 90-day upheld route disputes = 0).
ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen: the only chat message [F8] is a route-arrangement proposal ("mind if I go round via Zion Road?"); the rider's non-reply is not agreement, and the driver's post-trip statement [F10] is a claim, not rider consent (G11). No threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation anywhere in the complaint, chat or driver statement — safety_concern = none.

The passenger did not send any message before or during the trip; the record contains only the driver's 18:30 proposal [F8], [F9]. The off-route segment ran 18:34–18:45 [F3], i.e. after the driver's own message, and the rider never replied — so there is no consent for that segment. Ground: consent_after_or_none (RD-5) → the segment counts.

RD-4 was screened: traffic facts show only speed bands (Kampong Bahru band 2 [F11], New Bridge Road and Sentosa Gateway band 3 [F12][F13]) and no traffic incidents on the route [F14]; band data alone does not exempt a segment (RD-4(b) is corroborative only, MVP does not exempt on it alone), and the incident branch RD-4(a) is not met.

RD-2 (RydeTAXI branch): the unexempt segment added 4.45 km [F3]; the excess-distance component of the fare for the detour is 5.30 km × $1.4098/km = $7.47 [F4], billed within the $18.37 distance charge [F7]. Only the mileage unit is refunded; the in-trip stop/wait component ($0.11 [F5], 0.4 min × $0.26/min) is not refunded (RD-3(c): metered waiting is legitimately charged for RydeTAXI), and no other unpublished add-ons appear in the fare breakdown [F7]. Refund = $7.47, awarded as a Ryde voucher (NS-7).

RD-6 not triggered: driver's 90-day profile shows route disputes upheld = 0 [F17], so no account flag.

segment_findings.reason: The only rider-side record is the driver's own 18:30 message proposing an alternative via Zion Road [F8]; the rider never replied. The off-route segment (18:34–18:45, +4.45 km) therefore has no consent from the rider before it began. The driver's post-trip claim that the rider did not object [F10] is a claim, not consent (RD-5/G11). No rider-named stop (RD-3(a)) and no traffic incident on the replaced optimal route [F14]; band data alone does not exempt (RD-4(b)). The segment counts under RD-1/RD-2.

rejected_claims.reason: Driver's statement that the rider had 'no objection' is an unrecorded verbal-consent claim; only the rider's own message counts as consent (RD-5/G11), and there is no rider message at all.
Band 2 on Kampong Bahru Road is traffic-band evidence only; band data cannot exempt a segment on its own (RD-4(b)), and no matched traffic incident exists [F14].
